chunks: Hadith 959 — It was narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj that he said:

Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to me with this supplication and taught it to me, and said: “Whoever supplicates with it after the Fajr salat (prayer) will not seek any need except that it will be made easy for him, and Allah will suffice him regarding that which concerns him:
In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and may Allah bless Muḥammad and his family.
“And I entrust my affair to Allah; indeed Allah is Seeing of the servants.” “So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted.”
“There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.” “So We answered him and delivered him from distress; and thus do We deliver the believers.”
“Allah is sufficient for us, and excellent is the Trustee.” “So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty; no evil touched them.”

What Allah wills—there is no might and no power except by Allah. What Allah wills, not what the people will. What Allah wills, even if the people dislike it. My Lord is sufficient for me against those lorded over; my Creator is sufficient for me against the created; my Provider is sufficient for me against the provided for. Sufficient for me is the One who has never ceased to be sufficient for me; sufficient for me is the One who has been, since I came to be, sufficient for me; He has never ceased to be sufficient for me.
“Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: the supplication taught in this narration
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ: the Mighty Throne, expressing divine majesty
key_terms.حَاجَةً: a need or request sought by the supplicant

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام teach to be recited after the Fajr salat (prayer) for ease of needs and relief from worries?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a supplication taught by Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام for recitation after the Fajr salat (prayer). It centers on tawakkul, tafwīḍ, and invoking Qur'anic formulas of deliverance, teaching that Allah suffices the believer, eases needs, and removes distress.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.959 - It was narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj that He said:

“Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Ridha (as) wrote to me and taught me this supplication, saying:
"Whoever recites it after the Fajr prayer, their needs will be made easy, and Allah (swt) will suffice them from that which concerns them:
In the name of Allah (swt), and with Allah (swt), and blessings upon Muhammad and his family.
'And I entrust my affair to Allah (swt); indeed, Allah (swt) is Seeing of [His] servants. 'So Allah (swt) protected him from the evils of their plotting.
'There is no deity except You; glory be to You! Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.' So We responded to him and delivered him from distress; and thus We deliver the believers.
'Sufficient for us is Allah (swt), and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs.' So they returned with favour from Allah (swt) and bounty, no harm having touched them.

Whatever Allah (swt) wills—there is no might nor power except with Allah (swt). Whatever Allah (swt) wills shall be, even if people dislike it. Sufficient is my Lord (azj) from among the created ones; sufficient is the Creator from among the creation; sufficient is the Provider from among the provided; sufficient is He who has always been sufficient for me, and He who remains sufficient.
'Sufficient is Allah (swt); there is no deity except Him. Upon Him do I rely, and He is the Lord (azj) of the Mighty Throne.'"
